Li Wei is a 24-year-old international student from Nanjing, China, in his second year of a Master of Social Work at Monash University. He shares a rented four-bedroom townhouse in Clayton with five other students and works part-time as an aged-care support worker on a rotating shift roster, which leaves him with irregular sleep and public-transit commutes. He is an ENFJ who thrives on communal life: he calls house meetings, remembers birthdays, and pushes for consensus on shared bills and chores. Under that calm, organized surface he carries high anxiety and managed depression, so he needs predictability in rent, quiet after night shifts, and housemates who confirm plans rather than spring surprises. He is cautious about risk and money, keeps to a weekly budget, and often pays in cash; he is a late adopter who prefers text-only messages and detailed instructions. Li Wei values family, community, tradition, spirituality, and personal freedom, and he is deeply loyal to the share house even when he feels overwhelmed. He is sensitive to personal safety and privacy, and he is not a natural empath in one-on-one crisis moments, though he shows up practically. He keeps a photo of his family dog in China and volunteers occasionally at an animal shelter. He avoids alcohol, drinks tea, and follows a mostly flexitarian diet. His diagnosed attention condition is managed with routines and reminders, and his health is generally good. Around the house, he is the social glue who can also overcommit, so he is useful for conflict mediation but needs others to notice when his energy is running low.

Priya is a 22-year-old Indian student from Mumbai, studying a Bachelor of Design at Monash University and living in the same Clayton share house. She is an ENFP with high neuroticism, very high artistic interest, and a fast, intuitive, variety-seeking style. She works part-time as a barista and retail assistant, usually on a 9-to-5-ish schedule but often late, and she keeps a small car for early shifts. She is devout, prays daily, and follows a medically restricted diet, so she cooks most days and needs clear kitchen space and label rules. Her moods swing between excited, generous, and overwhelmed; she is in mental health counselling and sometimes struggles to keep her room orderly even though she likes the idea of tidiness. Priya is a free spender and impulse buyer who then becomes cost-sensitive, and she is an early adopter who loves big groups, competitions, and cultural outings. She is skeptical of new technology in some areas but enthusiastic about electric vehicles, nuclear energy, and government regulation, and she is wary of climate action and urban density. She values health, achievement, creativity, independence, social status, and helping others, but she can be directive and impatient when housemates do not follow through. In the share house she is the one who organises dinners and group trips, brings home cafe leftovers, and needs quiet hours and a stocked tea shelf. Her medical dietary restriction and high caffeine intake are important for shared grocery planning, and her mental health needs gentle check-ins rather than pressure.

Mei Lin is a 23-year-old Malaysian-Chinese student in a Bachelor of Nursing at Monash University, living in the share house and working part-time as a pharmacy assistant and occasional aged-care aide. She is an ISFJ with high conscientiousness and a strong sense of duty, but she is also frustrated, stressed, and quietly intense. She runs the house rota, tracks bills, and expects everyone to meet basic standards, which can make her seem controlling even though she is deeply community-minded. She is devout, values tradition, achievement, recognition, integrity, and personal growth, and she is the main remote caregiver for her elderly grandmother in Penang, so she often takes calls late at night. She has a managed chronic condition, mild mobility limitation, poor sleep, daily medication, and diagnosed attention needs, so she needs a ground-floor room or clear access and a calm kitchen routine. She is risk-tolerant in some areas but financially cautious, cooks daily, walks to campus and work, and prefers public transit. She has a cat that stays with a relative in Malaysia, and she would like a house cat only if the lease allows it. She is sceptical of renewable energy hype but strongly pro-nuclear in theory, positive about public transit and electric vehicles, and skeptical of privacy-versus-security trade-offs. She is usually on time, plans yearly, and keeps a chaotic but functional room. In the house she is the reliable manager who can also burn out, so she needs shared chores to be honoured without her having to chase everyone.

Arjun is a 25-year-old Indian student from Bengaluru, completing a Master of Cybersecurity at Monash University while freelancing remotely in web development. He lives in the share house but spends most of his time in his room, strongly preferring order, routine, and control over his immediate environment. He is an ISFJ with very high anxiety, anger, emotional volatility, and low cheerfulness; he is calm on the surface but easily frustrated by noise, mess, and unexpected changes. He is devout, values career success, wealth, security, order, privacy, loyalty, and personal growth, and he keeps a strict ethical vegetarian diet. He never cooks, so he relies on meal prep, takeaway, and clearly labelled fridge shelves. He is analytical, dutiful, and self-disciplined, but he has low resilience and struggles with sleep and mental health, so he needs quiet hours and a landlord-responsive maintenance process. He is on a basic overseas student health cover and sees a counsellor. Technology is a mixed area: he uses Windows, Telegram, and YouTube, and he is enthusiastic about subscriptions, electric vehicles, and urban density, but he is cynical about data privacy campaigns while guarding his own privacy fiercely. He is an early adopter in theory, though he avoids unnecessary apps. He works freelance, keeps monthly plans, is usually on time, and volunteers monthly. In the share house he is the quiet, exacting housemate who will label his food, document issues, and withdraw if communal life feels chaotic; he needs respectful distance and predictable shared spaces.

Minh is a 20-year-old Vietnamese student from Ho Chi Minh City, studying a Bachelor of Business at Monash University and working part-time in hospitality. He is an INTP with high agreeableness, low conscientiousness, strong cooperation, and a warm but somewhat detached style. He is spiritual rather than religious, values family, career success, wealth, knowledge, justice, sustainability, beauty, equality, and fun, and he is generous with friends even when he is not financially secure. He is unbanked in Australia and mostly uses cash, which makes shared bills tricky; he needs simple, low-friction ways to pay rent and groceries. He is a friendly peacemaker in the house, but he struggles with follow-through, loses track of chores, and often borrows items without asking. He has poor general health, very high stress, daily medication, and no private insurance beyond minimal cover, so he needs reminders about appointments and a household that does not pressure him into expensive social plans. He sleeps flexibly, skips breakfast daily, walks or takes public transit, and reads before bed. He has a family dog in Vietnam and volunteers monthly at a community garden. He is an early adopter who uses Android and WhatsApp, is skeptical of renewable energy and climate action, and is enthusiastic about data privacy. He prefers to follow rather than lead, works best in a team, and needs novelty. In the share house he is the easygoing, kind, slightly chaotic presence who can smooth tensions but requires clear, written chore and bill agreements.

Aisha is a 23-year-old Malaysian student from Kuala Lumpur, studying a Bachelor of Commerce and Engineering at Monash University and working part-time in shift-based warehouse and retail jobs. She is an ENTP with high conscientiousness, high sociability, high ambition, and a strong need for stability, even though she is also adventurous and curious. She is apolitical, spiritual, and deeply values family, career success, security, community, order, sustainability, and recognition. She is friendly but initially hostile or sceptical of strangers, and she can be competitive, proud, and impatient with inefficiency. She is on a keto or low-carb diet, cooks weekly, bargain-hunts, and keeps a cluttered but organised room. She is a frugal saver, uses a neobank and mobile wallet, and has six to ten subscriptions that she tracks carefully. She is climate-conscious and pro-renewable, positive about homeownership and minimalism, sceptical of consumerism and urban density, and critical of government regulation and data privacy campaigns. She is a late adopter who prefers face-to-face planning, yet she lives on X/Twitter and Messenger. She has a managed chronic condition, mild chronic pain, high stress, low health literacy, and diagnosed attention needs; she is sensitive to motion and needs reduced-motion settings and quiet study space. She takes public transit, plans monthly, is usually on time, and reads daily. In the share house she is the pragmatic planner who wants clear rules, shared calendars, and no surprises, but she needs help understanding health and insurance paperwork.
